title: Global existence and uniform-in-time boundedness for the 2D chemotaxis-fluid system with double chemical signals under a sub-logistic source (Theorem 1.1)
author: Shengquan Liu, Dongpu Li, Jiashan Zheng
work: Existence and boundedness of the classical global solution to 2D chemotaxis-fluid system with double chemical signals
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026, No. 10, pp. 1--22; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.10; publisher version
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the main result of the article: for any real chemotaxis and signal coefficients the two-dimensional chemotaxis-Stokes system with double chemical signals and a sub-logistic source admits a unique global classical solution that is bounded uniformly in time, under an explicit smallness condition coupling the chemical sensitivities, the initial signal bound, the Poincare and Gagliardo-Nirenberg constants and the constant mu that measures the logarithmic sub-logistic growth. The complete proof is a genuine bootstrap: it must extract the L1 bound on the cell density from the sub-logistic source through the infimum representation of the constant M, propagate it to Lp bounds on the velocity through the smoothing of the Stokes equation, obtain the entropy-like estimate for n log n together with the dissipation of the gradients of c, v and u, upgrade to Lp bounds on c and to a gradient estimate on c by the Neumann heat semigroup, and then close the L-infinity bound on n by a Moser-type iteration whose constants only close when the printed smallness condition holds; the extendibility alternative of the local existence lemma converts the resulting uniform bound into global existence. This multi-level a priori bootstrap with sharp constant tracking in a doubly cross-diffusive system is research level, well above an ordinary PhD qualifying examination, so the item is graded H3.
